auth_architecture: DECISION: Use Sanity's OWN authentication with multi-user login + roles managed in manage.sanity.io (Editor/Admin). Do NOT build a separate user store or shared password. Do NOT expose an all-powerful server write token to the browser. Writes must execute AS THE LOGGED-IN SANITY USER so per-user roles + audit trail apply. Mechanism: a browser @sanity/client configured with { withCredentials: true, useCdn: false, apiVersion: '2024-01-01', projectId, dataset } so it sends the Sanity session cookie on queries, mutations and asset uploads - the browser acts as the logged-in user. Auth state is verified via client.request({ url: '/users/me' }) (returns the logged-in user or 401). Unauthenticated users are sent to Sanity's hosted login. REQUIRED user step: in manage.sanity.io > API > CORS Origins, the app origins (http://localhost:3000, the vercel URL, https://coinscribed.com) MUST have 'Allow credentials' CHECKED (README already lists these for read; credentialed WRITE must be confirmed). Server routes under app/api/admin/* may PROXY but must forward/preserve the user's Sanity credential (e.g. pass through the session), never substitute a master token. If the coder finds cookie-based cross-site credentials unreliable for writes in this setup, the documented fallback is Sanity's login/token session flow that still yields a USER token (not a project-wide deploy token) - but the default target is withCredentials cookie auth. Document the exact chosen mechanism and any limitation unverifiable due to no-install sandbox.
